questions.question: What does an applicant have to submit in the ScotWind leasing round?
questions.truth: Crown Estate Scotland, ScotWind Leasing April 2019 update.

baseline.answer:
The ScotWind leasing round requires applicants to submit several key documents and information. I will present this information as per the technical documents found. </thinking>
Here is what an applicant has to submit in the ScotWind leasing round, according to the ScotWind Leasing - April 2019 update (working draft), p.2:

- Project concept
- Project delivery plan
- Capability and experience
- Development budget
- Developer financial resources
- Commitment to the project and preparedness

Additionally, applicants may be asked to complete an application form and provide separate substantive documents, including those outlined in Table 1 of the ScotWind Leasing - April 2019 update (working draft), p.2. If an application involves more than one legal entity, statements of commitment at board level are required (ScotWind Leasing - April 2019 update (working draft), p.2).

You can find more details in the ScotWind Leasing - April 2019 update (working draft): https://www.crownestatescotland.com/sites/default/files/2023-07/scotwind-leasing-april-2019-update.pdf

final.answer:
An applicant in the ScotWind leasing round must submit the following:

1. **Project concept**: A clear and detailed description of the proposed project, including the project's objectives, scope, and key features.

2. **Project delivery plan**: A comprehensive plan outlining the steps and timeline for the project's development, including key milestones and activities required to achieve the project's goals.

3. **Capability and experience**: Evidence of the applicant's relevant experience, expertise, and capabilities to successfully deliver the project. This may include past projects, technical expertise, and organizational capacity.

4. **Development budget**: A detailed budget for taking the project to the stage of securing key project consents for both the offshore and onshore elements. This budget should align with the preliminary feasibility study and the project delivery plan.

5. **Developer financial resources**: Information about all organizations responsible for funding the project, including their financial status and ability to secure the required funds on a timely basis.

6. **Statements of commitment**: Statements of commitment from the Lead Applicant and any Project Partners, at board level or equivalent, confirming their knowledge of and willingness to participate in the project, the availability of resources, and any other necessary commitments.

7. **Nearby windfarm tenants**: If the proposed project is within 5km of an existing offshore windfarm, documentary evidence of the existing tenant's consent to the proximity of the new project.

8. **Additional documents**: Depending on the specific requirements of the leasing round, applicants may be asked to provide additional documents such as a detailed development budget, information about all organizations responsible for funding the project, and statements of commitment from the Lead Applicant and any Project Partners.

These requirements are outlined in the ScotWind Leasing - April 2019 update document (leasing_round, p.1-5).

questions.diagnosis: Right six areas, but leaked a '</thinking>' tag and a sentence of planning. Later runs also padded each item with invented explanations, or returned an empty answer.
questions.fix: Reasoning tags stripped, a rule against explanations the page doesn't give, and one retry on an empty reply. It held on one final run, but the re-run after set 2 padded the six areas again ('A clear and detailed description of the proposed project...'): the padding comes from the tool's own answer, and the no-padding rule doesn't hold reliably on Nova Lite.

questions.question: What rules did the Hollandse Kust (zuid) permit set to protect bats?
questions.truth: HKZ PSD p.33: cut-in 5.0 m/s at axis height 15 Aug-30 Sep, 1 h after sunset to 2 h before sunrise; below it under 1 rpm.

baseline.answer:
The Hollandse Kust (zuid) permit set the following rules to protect bats:

1. The cut-in wind speed of turbines will be 5.0 m/s at axis height during the period of 15 August to 30 September between 1 hour after sunset to 2 hours before sunrise (Hollandse Kust (zuid) Wind Farm Sites I and II - Project and Site Description, p.33).
2. In case of a wind speed of less than 5.0 m/s at axis height, during the period referred to in part a, the permit holder will reduce the number of rotations per minute per wind turbine to less than 1 (Hollandse Kust (zuid) Wind Farm Sites I and II - Project and Site Description, p.33).
3. Within two months after the end of the period referred to in part a, the permit holder will produce a report outlining how and in which way this regulation is implemented and submit it to the Minister of Economic Affairs (Hollandse Kust (zuid) Wind Farm Sites I and II - Project and Site Description, p.33).

These rules were set under WFSD I and II Reg. 4.4 (Hollandse Kust (zuid) Wind Farm Sites I and II - Project and Site Description, p.33).

final.answer:
The Hollandse Kust (zuid) permit set the following rules to protect bats:

1. The cut-in wind speed of turbines will be 5.0 m/s at axis height during the period of 15 August to 30 September between 1 hour after sunset to 2 hours before sunrise (Hollandse Kust (zuid) Wind Farm Sites I and II - Project and Site Description (October 2017), p.33).
2. In case of a wind speed of less than 5.0 m/s at axis height, during the period referred to in part a, the permit holder will reduce the number of rotations per minute per wind turbine to less than 1 (Hollandse Kust (zuid) Wind Farm Sites I and II - Project and Site Description (October 2017), p.33).
3. Within two months after the end of the period referred to in part a, the permit holder will produce a report outlining how and in which way this regulation is implemented and submit it to the Minister of Economic Affairs (Hollandse Kust (zuid) Wind Farm Sites I and II - Project and Site Description (October 2017), p.33).

These rules were set under WFSD I and II Reg. 4.4 (Hollandse Kust (zuid) Wind Farm Sites I and II - Project and Site Description (October 2017), p.33).

questions.diagnosis: The bat curtailment rules, cited p.33.

questions.question: Which turbines are suspected of an anemometer calibration problem, and why?
questions.truth: Live analysis anomalies (rotor 82.4 m): only HillOfTowie_18, peak Cp above Betz with its power curve displaced +0.31 m/s from the farm mean. HillOfTowie_16 was also flagged until the rotor fix.

baseline.answer: Turbine HillOfTowie_18 is suspected of an anemometer calibration problem.
